messages.subject: Interrupt Rserve calculation instead closing connection
messages.subject_clean: Interrupt Rserve calculation instead closing connection
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 
i use Rserve from within a running R session (http://www.rforge.net/doc/packages/Rserve/run.Rserve.html) on Linux . I would like to interrupt a running R calculation. This isn't a problem if i return in the same process to R. However if i send the signal (SIGINT with Ctrl+c) if Rserve is running it closes the connection which i would like to avoid.
 
Is there a way to send an interrupt signal without to close the Rserve connection (e.g. interrupt Rserve calculation)?

Thanks in advance for any information.
 
 

_______________________________________________

stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de

messages.subject: Re: Interrupt Rserve calculation instead closing connection
messages.subject_clean: Interrupt Rserve calculation instead closing connection
messages.body_plain:
Marcel,

can you give more specifics? Rserve doesn't close the connection on interrupt - it only closes if R has exited. We do use SIGINT routinely to interrupt computations in Rserve sessions, so this will likely have something to do with your code or R settings. The normal behavior is to simply send evaluation error:

> c = RS.connect()
> pid = RS.eval(c, Sys.getpid())
> system(paste("sleep 5 && kill -INT", pid, "&"))
> RS.eval(c, Sys.sleep(10))
Error in RS.eval(c, Sys.sleep(10)) : 
  command failed with status code 0x1: error in R during evaluation
> RS.eval(c, getwd())
[1] "/private/tmp/Rserv/conn54023"

the connection is still well alive after that.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: RcallMethod: cannot determine object class in .jcall
messages.subject_clean: RcallMethod: cannot determine object class in .jcall
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

thanks for your answer.

I used .jaddClassPath to add the directory, where my .class file is located
on my hard  drive. However, I still get the 

    RcallMethod: cannot determine object class

error in

    .jcall("main/RAEBuilder.class","V","main")

Interestingly, after modifying the object parameter to a class which
definitely doesn't exist, I get a 

  ClassNotFoundException

Kind regards,

Ralph

-----Ursprüngliche Nachricht-----
Von: Simon Urbanek [mailto:simon.urbanek at r-project.org] 
Gesendet: Freitag, 30. Januar 2015 14:57
An: Ralph Fehrer
Cc: stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
Betreff: Re: [stats-rosuda-devel] RcallMethod: cannot determine object class
in .jcall

Ralph,

the error means that your class cannot be loaded - typically because it is
not on the class path - use .jaddClassPath() to add either the root
directory of your class structure or the jar file containing the class.
Another common issue is a JVM version mismatch - make sure your classes have
been compiled with a JVM version not higher than what you load from R
(check, e.g., with  J("java.lang.System")$getProperty("java.version")).

But if you fix that you will get

Error in .jcall("main/RAEBuilder","V","main")
  method main with signature ()V not found

because you are trying to call void main() method but you only have void
main(String[]), so you either want to create main() or use something like

.jcall("main/RAEBuilder","V","main", .jarray(character()))

Cheers,
Simon

Ralph,

.jaddClassPath(Sys.glob("c://MyProject/MyJars/*.jar"))

>  
>     .jpackage(name, jars='*', morePaths='', nativeLibrary=FALSE, lib.loc=NULL)
>  
> But I’m not really sure how to use it correctly.


You don't - that command is special for packages, it locates JARs in a specific package, not random places.
